summary: SDK errors missing request_id (and sometimes status_code) making support/oncall triage slow
description:
Issue summary:
Support + Eng Oncall are regularly unable to correlate customer-reported SDK errors to server-side logs because request_id is not consistently included in SDK-raised exceptions.

Impact:
- Slower time-to-triage (often 20–40 min longer per escalation).
- Higher back-and-forth with customers ("can you reproduce with debug logs?"), especially for intermittent 429/5xx and streaming disconnects.
- Oncall cannot quickly pivot to platform logs without request_id; forces broad log searches by timestamp/customer which is noisy.

What we need:
- All SDKs (Python/TS/Go) should surface request_id on every error thrown/returned from the client, including:
  1) Non-streaming responses with JSON error bodies
  2) Streaming responses where the connection drops mid-stream
  3) Network failures where there is no HTTP response (should be explicit: request_id unavailable)
- request_id should be exposed in a standard field name (request_id) and included in toString()/message only in a safe way (no secrets).
- When available, include status_code and error_code as well.

Notes / examples observed:
- TS: Some errors include headers but do not reliably map x-request-id into the thrown error shape.
- Python: For streaming iterator exceptions, we often see a generic "Stream disconnected" without request_id even when gateway logs show one.
- Go: Some error types surface StatusCode but not RequestID.

Acceptance criteria (supportability):
- Support can ask for "request_id" as a standard question; customers can paste it from the thrown exception object or logs.
- request_id is present in SDK errors for all HTTP error responses (4xx/5xx) and best-effort for streaming errors.
- Conformance tests cover request_id propagation in: 429, 500, invalid auth (401), and streaming disconnect scenario.

References:
- Related support escalations: SUP-29410 (Python streaming timeouts) and SUP-29505 (streaming disconnects behind proxy)
- Slack context: #eng-oncall discussion on request_id capture (see thread 1768161022)
- SDK parity workstream: ENG-5126 (cross-language error taxonomy) + ENG-5130 (gateway consistency)

Owner request:
Assign to SDK parity tech lead to fold into taxonomy + conformance suite; loop in platform if gateway header propagation is inconsistent.
comments: 2026-01-29 10:14 PT — Owen Phillips (Reporter): We’re missing request_id in multiple SDK error paths. This blocks us from searching gateway logs quickly. Recent oncall escalation spent ~45 min narrowing down a 429 spike because customer only had a stack trace without request_id.

2026-01-29 10:31 PT — Dev Patel (Support partner): +1. Support macro currently asks for "x-request-id" from response headers, but customers using SDKs rarely have access to headers. We need the SDK to print/return request_id directly. This is a recurring issue in enterprise cases where they can’t enable verbose HTTP logging.

2026-01-29 11:02 PT — Ibrahim Khan (Assignee): Acknowledged. This should be part of the cross-language error taxonomy (ENG-5126). We’ll standardize on request_id field and ensure we map x-request-id header and JSON error body field (if present). For streaming disconnects we’ll propagate last-seen request_id from initial response headers / first event if available.

2026-01-30 09:18 PT — Allison Grant (SRE/observability): From the SRE side, request_id is the key join between SDK telemetry and gateway logs. Please also add retry_count and attempt metadata to the same error surface (or at least to debug hooks) but primary requirement is request_id. If missing, error should say request_id=unknown rather than omitting the field entirely.

2026-02-03 14:27 PT — Dana Lo (TS owner): TS SDK currently attaches headers on the internal Response wrapper, but our Error class drops them in some branches (notably when body parse fails). I’ll align with error taxonomy PR (pr-1298) to always parse x-request-id and include it in RedwoodError.request_id.

2026-02-05 16:41 PT — Sabrina James (Python owner): Python streaming iterator throws a generic exception on disconnect; doesn’t include request_id. We can capture request_id from the initial HTTP response headers when establishing stream and attach it to StreamingDisconnectError. Will add to pr-854 follow-up or new patch.

2026-02-06 10:09 PT — Mateusz Zielinski (Go owner): Go error types have StatusCode and Body; RequestID is not plumbed. We’ll parse X-Request-Id header and add RequestID string to error. For mid-stream failures, we’ll return a typed error with RequestID if we had it at stream start.

2026-02-10 12:22 PT — Kaitlyn Nguyen (Platform/auth): Quick note: gateway sometimes emits request_id as both header x-request-id and JSON field request_id depending on endpoint and compat layer. Platform PR in flight to standardize (redwood/pr-28426). SDKs should treat header as source of truth, and JSON field as fallback for older paths.

2026-02-14 09:55 PT — Ibrahim Khan (Assignee): Update: Implementations landing across SDKs as part of parity. Also adding conformance fixture assertions: every simulated 4xx/5xx response must result in an error with request_id populated from header. Streaming fixture will assert request_id present on disconnect error when stream was established successfully.

2026-02-18 15:08 PT — Owen Phillips (Reporter): Verified in beta builds with a repro: 429 now surfaces request_id in error object in TS + Go; Python streaming disconnect now throws typed exception containing request_id captured from headers. This unblocks oncall log correlation. Marking resolved.
resolution:
Resolved via SDK parity work:
- Platform: standardized request_id propagation across gateway + downstream services (redwood/pr-28426).
- TypeScript: error shape now always includes request_id parsed from x-request-id header, including parse-failure branches (pr-1298).
- Python: streaming disconnect errors now include request_id captured at stream start; non-streaming errors include request_id consistently (pr-854).
- Go: added RequestID to error types; streaming errors include RequestID when available (pr-624).
- Conformance tests updated to assert request_id presence for HTTP error responses and best-effort for streaming disconnect scenarios.

Workaround prior to fix:
Ask customers to enable HTTP debug logging and capture response headers; this is no longer required for most cases.

Follow-ups:
- Ensure docs/support macros ask for request_id + SDK version.
- Ensure telemetry/logging fields include request_id consistently (ENG-5129).
